note:
THE RUNWAY WINDOW'S FIRST USE, AND THE NUMBER BEHIND IT WAS CORRECTED BEFORE IT REACHED HERE.

Seven heads of #627 reached `gate=success`. SIX OF THEM DID NOT MERGE. The seventh merged inside a four-minute runway window in which four armed pull requests were held; all four were re-armed afterwards with the reason printed.

The window doubled as its own live proof, with a control nobody arranged: the four held PRs stayed and an unheld armed PR merged in the same window.

WHY THE NUMBER IS SEVEN AND NOT FIVE. `dispatcher` first reported five and then decomposed their own figure rather than defending it: three verifiable SHAs, one reported-but-unnamed, and one directly observed -- three KINDS of evidence added into one integer and repeated four times. The query above replaced it, and the true number is larger than the one that could not be defended.

TWO PROPERTIES MAKE IT A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A TALLY, and both are the difference between this figure and a wrong one. `sort_by(.completed_at) | last`, never `first`: the check-runs list unions SUPERSEDED runs, so taking the first entry returns the OLDEST, and a count built on it would report some of these heads as failures. And heads with no `gate` conclusion at all are EXCLUDED rather than counted as failures -- eight of the eighteen never reached one, pushes superseded before CI finished. 'Never asked' and 'asked and failed' are different states, and folding them together would have been wrong in the other direction.
